_comment: Each group is a SHAPE class, not an owner. Regexes see shapes, so two
identifiers belong to the same group when they look alike to a regex —
RFC numbers and Bugzilla IDs are both 'bare-numeric' even though they come
A pattern matching probes from more than max_groups distinct groups is
accepting identifiers it has no business accepting. That is the defect this
corpus exists to catch: a CCM control pattern must not also swallow CVE IDs.
Legitimate cross-source overlap stays under the threshold by construction —
every CVE-shaped probe is in one group, so a CVE pattern matching all of
them scores 1 no matter how many namespaces publish CVE data.

note: Tokens no identifier scheme would ever issue. Matching ANY of these is a
violation on its own, regardless of group count.
Coverage matters as much as content. The first version of this list held
only long lower/mixed-case tokens, so ^[A-Z&]{2,3}$ sailed through and
secid:control/FOO returned seven fabricated results in production. Short
all-uppercase and short all-lowercase forms are therefore mandatory: a
nonsense probe only tests the patterns whose length and character class it

alpha-dash-numeric-control.note: NIST 800-53 and CSA CCM control IDs

ampersand-control.note: CCM domains containing '&' — the encoding edge case

note: PCI DSS requirements, ISO clauses, ISMAP controls (incl. the .P/.B/.PB
suffix form), and arXiv IDs. These are ONE group on purpose: to a regex
'2303.08774' and '9.2.3.11' are the same shape, and no pattern can tell
an arXiv paper from a PCI requirement by form alone. Splitting them made
ISMAP's correct pattern score three groups and fail.

doi.note: Distinct shape from dotted-numeric — contains a slash

kebab-slug.note: URL slugs used by CSA artifacts, NDSS papers, and similar

brand-word.note: Bare source/organisation names — what a human types into search
